title: Does dark mode really save battery?

segments.text: Does dark mode really save battery?
On some screens, it barely makes a difference.
Many older phones use LCD screens. A backlight shines behind the whole screen, and the pixels just block the light. So even black costs power.
Many newer phones use OLED. Here, every pixel makes its own light, and a black pixel is simply switched off.
So how much does that save? University researchers measured it on OLED phones.
At normal indoor brightness, dark mode saved only about three to nine percent.
At full brightness, about forty percent.
So dark mode pays off most in bright sunlight. Indoors, turning your brightness down can save just as much.
Is your phone in dark mode right now?

sources: Purdue University news release, 28 Jul 2021, 'Dark mode may not save your phone's battery life as much as you think, but there are a few silver linings' (official release on the Dash & Hu study), https://engineering.purdue.edu/ECE/News/2021/dark-mode-may-not-save-your-phones-battery-life-as-much-as-you-think-but-there-are-a-few-silver-linings (same text: https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/923727): 'At 30%-50% brightness, Purdue researchers found that switching from light mode to dark mode saves only 3%-9% power on average for several different OLED smartphones.'; 'switching from light mode to dark mode at 100% brightness saves an average of 39%-47% battery power'; auto-brightness indoors 'around 30%-40% most of the time'; apps: Google Maps, News, Phone, Calendar, YouTube, Calculator on Pixel 2, Moto Z3, Pixel 4, Pixel 5

Same release: 'Smartphones that came out after 2017 likely have an OLED (organic light-emitting diode) screen. Because this type of screen doesn't have a backlight like the LCD (liquid crystal display) screens of older phones, the screen will draw less power when displaying dark-colored pixels.' (basis for 'many older phones use LCD', 'many newer phones use OLED', and that dark pixels save power on OLED but not via a backlight on LCD)

Same release: 'Using the Google News app in light mode at 20% brightness on the Pixel 5, for example, draws the same amount of power as when the phone is at 50% brightness in dark mode.' (basis for 'Indoors, turning your brightness down can save just as much' and the payoff bars)

Peer-reviewed paper: P. Dash, Y. C. Hu, 'How much battery does dark mode save? An accurate OLED display power profiler for modern smartphones', ACM MobiSys 2021, pp. 323-335, https://doi.org/10.1145/3458864.3467682 (abstract: 'By omitting external lighting, OLED display significantly reduces the power draw compared to its predecessor LCD'). Full PDF not reachable from our environment (Cloudflare challenge); numbers taken from the university's release above.

LG, 'LG Screen Technology' explainer, https://www.lg.com/hk_en/lg-experience/helpful-hints/screen-technology-explained: LCD backlights 'are placed evenly behind the screen to deliver consistent light across the whole panel'; OLED panels 'don't require a backlight. In an OLED display, the sub-pixels light up when a voltage is applied'; 'the individual pixels can be turned off' (basis for the LCD cross-section and 'a black pixel is simply switched off')

Android Developers, Dark theme, https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/theming/darktheme: dark theme 'Reduces power usage by a significant amount, depending on the device's screen technology.' (supports 'on some screens it barely makes a difference' as screen-dependent)
